meta.title: Spring cleanup in Burton, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Grand Scapes does spring cleanups in Burton, MI: winter debris out, beds raked and edged, perennials cut back and the first cut done once the soft ground firms.

hero.title: A Burton yard, **cleared for spring.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes resets Burton yards each spring: sticks and matted leaves out, beds raked and edged, last year's perennials cut back, the salty strip by the walk looked over, and the first cut timed to the ground, so the beds are ready for mulch.

local.title: Soft lawns and **salt along the walk.**
local.intro: Most Burton springs bring two problems: a lawn that stays soft after the thaw, and a strip along the walk and drive that took all winter's ice melt. We work around the first and point out the second.

points.title: Wait for firm ground
points.body: MSU Extension warns that turning heavy mowers on saturated soil packs it and damages the turf. On Burton's slow draining ground that can mean a few dry days before the first cut, so we rake the beds first while the lawn firms up.

points.title: Salt damage by the walk
points.body: The city wants sidewalks cleared by 24 hours after every storm, and that usually means salt. MSU Extension says spring rain helps flush it from the soil, and watering helps in a dry spring. We point out the burned strip so you can decide what to do.

points.title: Dead wood now, shaping later
points.body: MSU Extension says spring bloomers like lilac, forsythia and spirea set their buds the summer before, so we take out dead wood in spring and save the shaping for after they bloom. See [shrub trimming in Burton](/shrub-trimming-burton-mi/).

points.title: Ditch banks after the thaw
points.body: Where a Burton street drains to a ditch, winter leaves sticks, leaves and road grit along the bank. We clear what sits on your side, so the first mow of the year is a clean one.

logistics.title: How a Burton spring cleanup runs.
body: Rob sets the date with you once the snow is gone and the ground can take foot traffic. Beds and hard surfaces come first, and the lawn gets its first cut when it is firm enough to mow without rutting.

The crew picks up sticks and debris, blows and rakes matted leaves out of the beds and corners, cuts back last year's perennials and ornamental grasses, recuts the bed edges and hauls everything away in our trailer. Walks and the drive get blown off at the end.
Most yards go straight from here into fresh [mulch](/mulch-installation-burton-mi/) and weekly [mowing](/lawn-mowing-burton-mi/).

facts.label: Timing
facts.value: After the thaw, once the ground firms

faq.q: Do you do spring cleanups in Burton?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does spring cleanups in Burton: sticks and leaves out, beds raked and cut back, edges recut, debris hauled away and the first mow done when the ground is ready. Rob comes out and quotes it free.

faq.q: When should spring cleanup happen in Michigan?
faq.a: Once the snow is gone and you can walk the lawn without sinking in. Raking and edging beds can start sooner, but mowing soaked ground packs the soil, which MSU Extension warns against. On slow draining soil, that often means waiting for a few dry days.

faq.q: Should I prune my shrubs in spring?
faq.a: Dead and broken branches, yes. Shaping depends on the plant. MSU Extension says lilac, forsythia, spirea, weigela and viburnum set next year's flowers the summer before, so cutting them back in early spring removes the blooms. Prune those right after they flower.

faq.q: What do I do about salt damage along the sidewalk?
faq.a: Start with water. MSU Extension says spring rain helps flush salt out of the soil, and in a dry spring watering the area helps. We point out the damaged strip during the cleanup, and the beds nearest the walk can be replanted with tougher plants.
